results.comment: Hopefully this will clear things up:   At the beginning of the year, they raised money by selling 1/3 of the equity in the company for $500 and also raised $250 through a debt issue. Cash balance: $750 = 500 + 250 They then spent $300 to buy the first stand and $200 on inventory (this is your cost of goods sold, or COGS). Cash balance: $250 = 750 - 300 - 200 At the end of year 1, we see they sold $800 of lemonade, and paid $530 in labor costs (remember, we already bought the inventory, and depreciation is a "non-cash" charge - we're accounting for having to replace the lemonade stand every 5 years). Cash balance: $520 = 250 + 800 - 530 Finally, they paid $25 in interest, leaving them with negative EBT (earnings before tax) of $15 and therefore had a tax credit of $5 (this was sort of skipped over): Cash balance: $500 = 520 - 25 + 5  Note this matches the ending cash balance (bottom line) in the cash flow statement at 8:15. With that, we have enough to spend $300 on a second lemonade stand with money to spare.
